description: Remove every hardcoded self-binary-name dependency from the code: auto-spawn resolves by execPath, process discovery stops comparing argv against a single name literal, and the self-invoke helper drops its own literal fallback.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Bun.spawn/Bun.spawnSync take `command: string[]` and use posix_spawn(3); cmd[0] is an executable path or name, so passing an absolute `process.execPath` is fully supported and needs no PATH lookup. An `argv0` option exists to override the argv[0] the child advertises, which is what other processes (and `ps -eo pid,args`) observe. No breaking changes or deprecations affecting this cycle.
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: Bun exposes `argv0` as a way to keep advertising a fixed name to `ps`, which would preserve stop.ts's current literal-name discovery; the local convention (execPath self-invoke, src/util/self-invoke.ts) instead makes the advertised argv0 vary by install path, so discovery must become name-agnostic rather than being pinned back with argv0.

userStories.title: WARNING: File-descriptor leak in the long-lived watcher process. makeSpawnSidec…
userStories.description: WARNING [src/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.ts:121]: File-descriptor leak in the long-lived watcher process. makeSpawnSidecarFn calls openSync(logPath,'a') INSIDE the returned closure, and nothing closes that fd. Unlike spawnSidecarDefault (src/commands/run.ts:857), which runs once per `cam run`, this closure runs on every respawn attempt, and handleOneTick resets state.attempts to 0 whenever the sidecar is observed alive again (lines 185-188), so a flapping sidecar accumulates descriptors without bound over a session's lifetime. Verified empirically by the reviewer rather than inferred: 5 openSync+Bun.spawn cycles left all 5 fds still open in the parent (scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3); Bun's spawn docs confirm `number` is a supported stdout/stderr value and that the child gets its own duplicate, so the parent copy is redundant after spawn. Mechanical 1-file fix: closeSync(logFd) immediately after the Bun.spawn call.

userStories.title: WARNING: The US-R4-001 regression test does not exercise the code US-R4-001 cha…
userStories.description: WARNING [test/integration/stop-defaultlistprocesses-real.test.ts:189]: The US-R4-001 regression test does not exercise the code US-R4-001 changed, so it is not falsifiable against that story's fix. The fix lives in makeSpawnSidecarFn (src/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.ts:118-125): open the sidecar log and hand the fd to Bun.spawn as stdout/stderr instead of 'ignore'. The test re-implements that shape in its own body (lines 189-194: buildSidecarRespawnArgv + a hand-rolled openSync + stdio:['ignore',logFd,logFd]) and never calls the production closure. makeSpawnSidecarFn is not exported, no test imports it, and test/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.test.ts always injects spawnSidecarFn, so the production default is never constructed anywhere in the suite. Reverting makeSpawnSidecarFn to stdio:['ignore','ignore','ignore'] leaves all 5935 tests green. The test does verify defaultListProcesses (which is useful and real-I/O), but it is not the regression guard the story claims. Mechanical fix: export makeSpawnSidecarFn (or expose the spawn through the existing DI seam) and assert against the real respawned process that it holds .claude/cam-supervisor.log open.

userStories.title: WARNING: Under-match regression, carried unfixed from round 3 and re-verified l…
userStories.description: WARNING [src/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.ts:105]: Under-match regression, carried unfixed from round 3 and re-verified live at Layer B this round. `makeSpawnSidecarFn` respawns the sidecar with `stdio: ['ignore','ignore','ignore']`, so that sidecar holds no fd on `.claude/cam-supervisor.log`. The new process-identity check in `defaultListProcesses` (src/commands/stop.ts:449-453) requires exactly that open fd, so a liveness-watch-respawned sidecar is invisible to `cam stop`'s fallback scoped scan and is silently left running in the one situation the fallback exists for (pid file absent or stale, e.g. after an earlier `cam stop` removed the pid file without the SIGTERM taking). main matched this class via `argv[0] === 'cam'`, so it is a regression. Reviewer's independent probe against the real ps+lsof production path (scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3): pid A (spawnSidecarDefault shape, holds the log open) matched and was SIGTERM'd; pid B (byte-for-byte the makeSpawnSidecarFn shape) matched=false. This also falsifies the universal invariant the identity check is justified by, asserted at src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts:20-27 ('Every real sidecar process holds this file open on fd 1/2 for its entire lifetime') and repeated at src/commands/stop.ts:403-406, and the decoy case in test/integration/stop-defaultlistprocesses-real.test.ts:89-92 codifies that exact production shape as a process that must NOT be matched. Mechanical 2-file fix: give the respawn the same `openSync(join(cwd,'.claude',SIDECAR_LOG_FILENAME),'a')` stdout/stderr redirection `spawnSidecarDefault` uses (src/commands/run.ts:856-860; Bun docs confirm a raw fd number is a supported stdout/stderr value), plus a regression case in test/integration/stop-defaultlistprocesses-real.test.ts asserting a liveness-watch-shaped respawn IS discovered.

userStories.title: CRITICAL: The false-positive class US-R1-001 was written to close is still OPEN…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [src/commands/stop.ts:330]: The false-positive class US-R1-001 was written to close is still OPEN, verified live at Layer B against the REAL production path (real `ps -eo pid,args` + real `lsof` via defaultListProcesses, killFn stubbed to record only): `Bun.spawn(['/usr/bin/tail','-F','sidecar'], {cwd})` still yields fallbackSidecarKilled=true and killFn receives the tail's pid (see scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3). That is the EXACT reproduction round 1 recorded as the CRITICAL, so the story's own cited evidence case is not fixed. `isSidecarArgv` accepts any argv with length >= 2 whose LAST token is the literal word 'sidecar' and whose argv[0] starts with '/', so the anchor only excludes hand-typed bare-name commands; every tool/agent/editor-spawned process uses an absolute argv[0] (`/opt/homebrew/bin/rg -n sidecar`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/bun test sidecar`, `/usr/bin/tail -F sidecar`), and in this repo `sidecar` is a routine grep/test filter term. The docstring's justifying claim (stop.ts:307-310, 'an interactive command ... is invoked via a bare PATH-relative name as argv[0], never an absolute path') is disproven by the runtime probe. main was immune (it required argv[0] === 'cam'), so this is a live regression: `cam stop` SIGTERMs unrelated processes. Argv shape alone cannot separate the two classes; close it with a process-identity check the fallback can afford (it already runs `lsof` per candidate), e.g. require the candidate pid to hold this project's sidecar artifact open (.claude/cam-supervisor.log / the sidecar pid file), which also closes the under-match in the WARNING below.

userStories.title: CRITICAL: isSidecarArgv over-matches and makes `cam stop` SIGTERM unrelated pro…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [src/commands/stop.ts:298]: isSidecarArgv over-matches and makes `cam stop` SIGTERM unrelated processes. The predicate accepts ANY argv of length 2 or 3 whose last token is the literal word 'sidecar', so any command running in the project cwd that happens to end in that word is classified as this project's sidecar and sent SIGTERM by the fallback scan (performStop step 1c, stop.ts:481-491). Proven at Layer B against the REAL production path (real `ps -eo pid,args` + real `lsof` via defaultListProcesses, killFn stubbed to record only): `Bun.spawn(['/usr/bin/tail','-F','sidecar'], {cwd})` yielded fallbackSidecarKilled=true and killFn received the tail's pid 58293 (see scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3). Realistic collisions in a dev cwd: `rg sidecar`, `tail -F sidecar`, `git log sidecar`. This is a regression: main anchored the match on record.argv[0] === 'cam', so no unrelated command could match. It also defeats the intent of US-004 acceptance criterion 2 case 4 ('a process in the project cwd that is not running the sidecar subcommand does NOT match'): the chosen fixture ['bun','/repo/index.ts','run'] passes while the whole false-positive class stays open. Fix by keeping name-agnosticism but re-anchoring on a property the real self-spawn always has and an ad-hoc command does not, e.g. require argv[0] to be an absolute executable path (both production shapes, [execPath,'sidecar'] and [runtime,script,'sidecar'], always carry one because Bun.spawn is handed process.execPath), and add a negative test for the ['tail','-F','sidecar'] / ['rg','sidecar'] class.

userStories.title: WARNING: The same predicate under-matches a real sidecar whose executable path…
userStories.description: WARNING [src/commands/stop.ts:336]: The same predicate under-matches a real sidecar whose executable path contains a space. defaultListProcesses splits the `ps` args column with `argsStr.split(/\s+/)`, and isSidecarArgv requires exactly 2 or 3 tokens; before this branch argv[0] was always the bare literal 'cam' so token count was stable, but US-002 now puts the full absolute execPath (and, interpreted, the full script path) into the ps line. An install under e.g. `/Users/x/My Tools/cam` produces 3+ tokens for the compiled shape and 4+ for the interpreted one, so the live sidecar becomes invisible to the fallback scan and `cam stop` silently leaves it running. The diff itself treats space-bearing paths as in-scope (test/integration/dashboard-pane-selfspawn.test.ts:74-76 deliberately uses 'cam script dir/run me.ts'), so the ps parser should tolerate them too (e.g. anchor on the last token plus an absolute-path prefix rather than an exact token count).

userStories.title: Drop the literal binary-name fallback from the self-invoke helper
userStories.description: As the loop driver, I need resolveSelfInvokeArgv to never emit a hardcoded product name, so that every self-spawn built on it resolves to the exact executable currently running instead of whatever the PATH happens to hold.
acceptanceCriteria: resolveSelfInvokeArgv carries no literal binary name, in the returned argv or in its docstring. [oracle: bash -c '! grep -qE "argv1 \?\? .cam." src/util/self-invoke.ts']

The degenerate interpreted-mode case (argv1 undefined) resolves to an execPath-only argv, the helper docstring states that shape, and the existing unit case for the old PATH-lookup fallback is rewritten to assert it. [oracle: bash -c '! grep -q "falls back to the bare" test/util/self-invoke.test.ts']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]

The quality spine passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]

PIN DE INVARIANCIA: os cinco contratos internos do ADR-0054 NAO renomeiam. As contagens de CAM_, .cam-, do socket tmux -L cam e de /cam- em src mais index.ts ficam identicas as da main, derivadas ao vivo e nao congeladas. findings.text: Layer B behavioral-gate FAIL (hard constraint): the 'PIN DE INVARIANCIA' oracle for the five internal ADR-0054 contracts is an acceptance criterion of US-001, US-002, US-003 and US-004 (all four recorded passes:true) and exits 1 on the reviewer's independent re-run. Three of the four patterns are at parity (CAM_ 164=164, .cam- 153=153, tmux -L cam 15=15) but /cam- is 205 on main vs 206 in the worktree, so `test "$b" = "$a"` fails. Per-file delta: src/commands/run.ts 16->15 (inline 'cam-supervisor.log' literal replaced by SIDECAR_LOG_FILENAME), src/commands/stop.ts 2->3 (new docstring line 403 spelling `.claude/cam-supervisor.log`), src/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.ts 0->1 (new docstring line 103 spelling `.claude/cam-supervisor.log`); net +1. This is a pure git/grep computation over committed trees, run twice with identical results: deterministic, not flaky, not environmental, not pre-existing on main. It was also raised as CRITICAL by the round-5 reviewer, left unfixed, and the cycle closed as MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT with the four stories still marked passes:true. Mechanical 2-file fix: have the two new docstrings name the shared SIDECAR_LOG_FILENAME constant instead of spelling the `.claude/cam-supervisor.log` path literally, restoring count parity. Full evidence in scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 2, ORACLE 11.

File-descriptor leak in the long-lived watcher process. makeSpawnSidecarFn calls openSync(logPath,'a') INSIDE the returned closure, and nothing closes that fd. Unlike spawnSidecarDefault (src/commands/run.ts:857), which runs once per `cam run`, this closure runs on every respawn attempt, and handleOneTick resets state.attempts to 0 whenever the sidecar is observed alive again (lines 185-188), so a flapping sidecar accumulates descriptors without bound over a session's lifetime. Verified empirically by the reviewer rather than inferred: 5 openSync+Bun.spawn cycles left all 5 fds still open in the parent (scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3); Bun's spawn docs confirm `number` is a supported stdout/stderr value and that the child gets its own duplicate, so the parent copy is redundant after spawn. Mechanical 1-file fix: closeSync(logFd) immediately after the Bun.spawn call.

The US-R4-001 regression test does not exercise the code US-R4-001 changed, so it is not falsifiable against that story's fix. The fix lives in makeSpawnSidecarFn (src/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.ts:118-125): open the sidecar log and hand the fd to Bun.spawn as stdout/stderr instead of 'ignore'. The test re-implements that shape in its own body (lines 189-194: buildSidecarRespawnArgv + a hand-rolled openSync + stdio:['ignore',logFd,logFd]) and never calls the production closure. makeSpawnSidecarFn is not exported, no test imports it, and test/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.test.ts always injects spawnSidecarFn, so the production default is never constructed anywhere in the suite. Reverting makeSpawnSidecarFn to stdio:['ignore','ignore','ignore'] leaves all 5935 tests green. The test does verify defaultListProcesses (which is useful and real-I/O), but it is not the regression guard the story claims. Mechanical fix: export makeSpawnSidecarFn (or expose the spawn through the existing DI seam) and assert against the real respawned process that it holds .claude/cam-supervisor.log open.

Carried unaddressed from rounds 1-5: bootstrapHub has no injectable spawnSync seam, so its exit-status mapping ((result.status ?? 1) === 0, including the signal-killed null case) has zero direct coverage, and the `if (cmd === undefined) return false` guard at line 41 is an unreachable branch that exists only to satisfy noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Injecting a spawnSync fn (as stop.ts already does with spawnSyncFn) makes the mapping testable and removes the dead branch. This is a new shared file, so the seam is cheaper to add now than after six proxies depend on it.

isSidecarArgv now carries a ~55-line docstring over a 3-line body, most of it a chronological narrative of the argv[0] anchor being added (US-R1-001) and then dropped (US-R2-002). The same narrative is already recorded verbatim in scripts/cam/patterns.md and in the file-size-budget _ref, and it accounts for a large share of the stop.ts 689 -> 799 ceiling raise. A short statement of the current contract plus a pointer would preserve the knowledge and recover most of the raise. The raise itself is documented in the _ref tracker, so this is not blocking.

Carried from earlier rounds: the four one-line self-spawn builders (buildDashboardRespawnArgv, buildSidecarSpawnArgv, buildRecycleWatchSpawnArgv, buildSidecarLivenessWatchSpawnArgv) are pure wrappers over buildSelfSpawnArgv with no run.ts dependency, and buildSidecarRespawnArgv in sidecar-liveness-watch.ts is a fifth copy of the same shape. Co-locating them in src/util/self-invoke.ts would avoid a large part of the run.ts 1169 -> 1222 ceiling raise on an already 1200-line file.

Residual under-match of the holdsSidecarLogOpen identity check, worth one docstring line so the next reader does not rediscover it as a defect: a sidecar launched by hand in a terminal (stdout on a tty, not redirected to .claude/cam-supervisor.log) is invisible to the fallback scoped scan, where main matched it via argv[0]==='cam'. Practical impact is low because runSidecar writes its own pid file at boot, so the pid-file route in step 1b covers that shape. Separately, expectedLogPath is compared with strict === against lsof's resolved names, so a symlinked .claude/ or a rotated log would also miss.

parseLsofOpenFiles has no direct unit test: its edge cases (an `n` line with no preceding `f` line, output with no `cwd` entry, trailing blank lines, a name containing whitespace) are only exercised indirectly through the real-lsof integration test, which cannot produce malformed input. A small pure-function test over fixture lsof text would give the parser its own success/error/edge triad with no I/O.

Knowledge-layer staleness in the appended bullets: the US-R1-002 bullet still points at 'the "[resolved 2026-08-02]" US-004 bullet above', a marker US-R1-004 removed, so the pointer no longer resolves; the US-004 bullet headline still reads 'length 2 or 3', which is no longer the predicate and is what a future grep hits first. Also, six of the twelve added lines use the em-dash character, which the project convention bans in persisted human-readable markdown (noted, not blocking, since main already carries 43 such lines in this file).
